correctness.rationale: The nonnegative coordinate faces are inward, and on H=0 one has H'=(C+B)/(1+128C^3)+T>=0. At equilibrium B=C and S=T=h(C), and the factored F has just the physical root 1/4. In (c,v,z,y) coordinates, the proposed V has derivative with cross-terms -(3/4)h'vy and -(3/4)vz. The bounds -1/3<=h'<=1 and g>=1/129 give v, y, z dissipation constants 8/3, 3/8, 125/1032 by Young's inequality. The only invariant set with zero dissipation is E, so LaSalle applies on the compact simplex. For the local result the stable (v,y) block has trace -53/12 and determinant 53/12, with the remaining stable eigenvalue -1/3 from z, and the zero direction is the c direction in these coordinates. On a center manifold chosen in z=0, the transverse linear operator is invertible, so the invariance equations eliminate terms of order two. The cubic forcing is F=32u^3+O(u^4), and the equations for v=a u^3+O(u^4), y=b u^3+O(u^4) give b=4a/3 and (53/12)a=-32. Thus (1/u^2)'=768/53+O(u) on either nonzero branch. Local exponential tracking by the stable foliation transfers the signed limit to the corresponding physical trajectories; the leaf tracking the zero center orbit is the three-dimensional strong-stable manifold. Global convergence makes this dichotomy applicable after a finite time for all initial states. Returning to original coordinates multiplies the scalar limit by (-1/3,1,1,-1/3). The bundled symbolic and numerical checker was inspected read-only; finite-time integrations are not evidence for the tracking theorem.
